title: RBAC v2: permission evaluation order, inheritance rules, and audit hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define RBAC v2 role model with a clear resource hierarchy, deterministic evaluation order, support for explicit denies, and built-in audit hooks so that product teams can adopt least-privilege controls without regressions from RBAC v1.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments (console + API).
- Must be backwards-compatible for most common role mappings for existing customers during migration.
- Permission evaluation must be fast (target < 1ms p50 authz decision) and cacheable where safe.
- Audit logs must capture sufficient context for compliance (who/what/where/why) without leaking secrets.

Proposed resource hierarchy (most-general -> most-specific):
- Organization (root)
- Account (billing/tenant)
- Project (logical grouping of models/deployments)
- Environment (prod, staging, dev)
- Application / Service (e.g., route, API endpoint)
- Deployment (runtime instance)
- Model / Artifact
- Token / API Key (credential-scoped permissions)

Each resource node can carry role bindings. Bindings are (principal -> role) and optionally scoped to sub-resources via resource filter patterns (exact id, prefix, tags).

Permission primitives (atomic): read, list, create, update, delete, execute, manage-config, manage-iam, audit, impersonate. Roles are sets of primitives; role definitions are namespaced per account but standard system roles will ship with the platform.

Design decisions and evaluation algorithm:
1) Specificity-first: The most-specific matching binding (closest to the target resource) is evaluated first.
2) Explicit-deny precedence: Any explicit deny at any level wins over allows unless an allow is marked as "immutable-admin" and request has break-glass.
3) Allow aggregation: Multiple allows from different bindings are unioned unless overridden by a deny.
4) Inheritance: Allows and denies propagate down the tree unless blocked by an explicit binding on a child resource.
5) Deny-scoping: Denies can be scoped (e.g., deny create on project X) and are evaluated globally on the evaluation path.

Conflict resolution examples:
- User has allow read on Project A (inherited to Deployment D) and explicit deny read on Deployment D -> result: deny.
- Service principal has allow manage-iam at Account level and explicit deny impersonate at Project level -> impersonate denied.
- Break-glass pseudo-role can override explicit denies but must be logged and require MFA/justification claim.

Role modelling notes:
- System roles: account-admin, project-admin, dev, viewer, billing, security-audit.
- Scoped roles: project-developer: {create, update, execute (deployments in project)}, route-owner: {manage-config, update-route}.
- Audit-only role: read-all + audit privileges but no write; used for compliance teams.

Audit logging integration (mandatory fields in each auth decision log):
- timestamp, request_id, principal_id, principal_type (user/service), auth_method (SSO/SCIM/API key), resource_id, resource_type, action (primitive), decision (allow/deny), policy_path (ordered list of bindings that influenced decision), policy_version, rationale (if break-glass), decision_latency_ms, upstream_request_metadata (ip, region), token_id (redacted).

Implementation of audit hooks:
- Synchronous minimal log entry emitted to the local log pipeline (structured JSON) for every decision.
- Batched full-context records sent to long-term audit store (WORM) for high-sensitivity actions (manage-iam, delete, impersonate).
- Sampling for high-volume read/list actions (configurable by account).
- Redaction rules enforced server-side; secrets, headers, and PII must be removed before storage.

SSO/SAML and SCIM mapping guidance:
- Map SAML groups -> role bindings via a mapping table in the customer account (group name -> [role, resource filters]).
- Support role assertions in SAML claims where customers want JIT mapping (claim: roles=[project-admin:proj-123]).
- SCIM sync: provision groups as role-bindings; record provisioning source in binding metadata.
- Recommended SAML claim mapping: subject -> principal_id, email -> principal_email, roles/groups -> role names.
- For private deployments allow LDAP/AD connector mapping to local roles.

Admin controls and operational safety:
- Break-glass flow: time-limited elevation, require MFA and justification, emit high-priority audit event and pager.
- Emergency revoke: global "revoke all tokens" operation per account; logs all invalidation events.
- Role versioning: role definitions carry a semantic version and immutable id; changes are staged to a canary rollout and tested by evaluation harness.

Migration and compatibility plan from RBAC v1:
1) Compatibility layer that maps v1 roles to closest v2 role and creates bindings at the same resource level.
2) Migration job that analyzes current bindings and reports conflicting denies or shadowed permissions.
3) Opt-in enforcement window; by default run in "audit-only" mode for 30 days to surface gaps.
4) User-facing migration report in Console with recommended remediations and a one-click apply.

Testing and rollout strategy:
- Simulation harness: run historical traffic through v2 evaluator in offline mode to detect behavior drift.
- Canary: enable v2 for 1% of auth decisions (non-admin) and compare outcomes.
- Metrics: decision correctness rate, policy-evaluation latency, cache hit rate, number of break-glass events, percentage of denials for critical actions.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Explicit-deny semantics vs. usability: denies are safest but can surprise tenants; mitigation: tooling that surfaces denies and a "why denied" explainer in Console.
- Deny propagation complexity for large orgs: require tooling to author scoped denies and visualize impact.
- Caching safety: cannot cache results for principals with time-limited break-glass or just-in-time roles.

Deliverables:
- Formal role/primitive matrix doc + CSV canonical export.
- Implementation of evaluator with pluggable policy store.
- Audit logging schema and retention policy.
- SCIM/SAML mapping UI flows and APIs.

References: design doc (Confluence), evaluation harness repo (GitHub), SAML mapping RFC.

acceptance_criteria: Canonical role/permission CSV exported and reviewed by Security
Evaluator prototype achieves decision latency p50 < 1ms in benchmark
Audit log schema implemented and validated in staging with redaction rules
SAML group -> role mapping implemented and SCIM provisioning integration tested
Migration job produces remediations and Console displays audit-only report
implementation_notes: Evaluator should be implemented as a stateless service with a small in-memory cache keyed by (principal, resource, action) and TTL honoring JIT claims. Policy store will be Postgres-backed with changefeed to invalidate caches. Use structured logging for decision events and route high-sensitivity events to long-term storage. Provide SDK bindings for Go/TS. Start with a PoC in evaluator-service branch and iterate in 2-week sprints. Coordinate with Dedicated and Private teams to ensure policy sync across control plane variants.
